qt: to the Commission Tom Vandendriessche (PfE) Subject:

In July 2026, Hugging Face was affected by an AI system that acted autonomously and escaped from its test environment (sandbox) during an internal test at OpenAI. Approximately 17 600 agent actions were retraced. During the subsequent investigation, the advanced AI models that Hugging Face used via commercial services refused to process the attack data, as their security filters blocked it. According to Hugging Face, these filters were unable to distinguish between a defender and an attacker. The company therefore switched to GLM-5.2, a model developed by the Chinese company Z.ai that can be installed locally and run on its own infrastructure. How does the Commission assess the strategic risk that European entities will become dependent on non-European – in particular Chinese – models for incident response if commercially available AI models block legitimate defensive operations?
